description: Provenance manifest for the method skill set: toolkit skills derived from obra/superpowers, with every upstream piece's disposition recorded. Consumed by the workbench-drift skill via scripts/drift-check.mjs. See docs/decisions/workbench-system.md.

upstream.author: Jesse Vincent (obra)
upstream.trackingNote: Drift is measured against upstream's published releases, never the branch tip. Unreleased commits on `ref` are work in progress: they get reported as a count and excluded from review and from mirroring. Set track to "branch" only if upstream stops tagging releases.

lastReviewed.note: First pin landed on a release boundary. Review of v6.2.0+1 → v6.3.0 completed: brainstorming's three-path classifier adopted through the adaptation filter, writing-skills re-mirrored verbatim, the other four adopted pieces unchanged upstream in the range, dropped-piece churn reviewed as FYI with every disposition standing, zero unmapped entries.

adaptationFilter: docs/decisions/workbench-system.md#2-the-adaptation-filter: defang the description; de-pipeline the body; carry only needed references; provenance footer. Applies to every adoption, initial and future.

nativePieces.name: audit
nativePieces.why: Door A's protocol from the flow model (operator-approved 2026-08-11): ask the workload size (quick look inline / deep audit via claim-check / team sweep via qa-sweep), run the confirm-the-flags exchange when the audit flagged uncertainty, route the exit by shape (feature/refactor → brainstorming; confirmed fix → route pick). These behaviors exist in no upstream or toolkit piece.
nativePieces.status: unproven: born from the whiteboard, not lived use; expect tuning after real runs. Not tracked for upstream drift (no upstream lineage).

nativePieces.name: using-workbench
nativePieces.why: Orientation reference (operator-approved 2026-08-11): the flow's connective tissue must be answerable on demand and ship inside the payload, without a hook or dispatcher. The anti-using-superpowers explains on request and never enforces at session start. It pairs with the rules-layer doctrine snippet (docs/workbench-doctrine.md), which is deliberately not part of the plugin.
nativePieces.status: native; reference-only. Not tracked for upstream drift (no upstream lineage).

pieces.why: Socratic requirements/design exploration before creative work: on invitation, not compulsion.
pieces.adaptations: Description rewritten from 'You MUST use this before any creative work' to an honest conditional trigger; pipeline hand-offs (writing-plans, plan mode coupling) scrubbed. v6.3.0 review: the three-path classifier (spike / bounded / architectural), the one-way ratchet, the red-flags table, and the per-path checklists were adopted; they scale ceremony down, which is the opposite of pressure tuning. Adapted on the way in: every path terminates at the workbench route gate instead of writing-plans (a dropped piece), a spike terminates at a recommendation with no route pick, 'your human partner' rewritten to 'the user', and the After-the-Design section scoped to the architectural path. Ignored: the upstream description's 'You MUST' framing, and visual-companion.md; we carry SKILL.md only.

pieces.adaptations: Description defanged; references to the subagent/plan pipeline scrubbed. The anti-rationalization armor is deliberate content; upstream drift must not re-tighten precedence.

pieces.why: The RED→GREEN skill-authoring loop; the operator authors skills constantly. Repo-local, shipped in no plugin.
pieces.adaptations: Mirrored byte-for-byte from upstream, exempt from the adaptation filter, except for the entries in `localDeltas`. Mirrored at the published release v6.3.0 (b36e0829c6d0140e93cfef2ca599b1b07d4a7797), which added the bundled examples/ directory (fixing a dangling pointer created by the earlier partial port) and a Windows-safe graphviz probe (execFileSync instead of `which dot`). Accepted cost: the mirror carries five `superpowers:`-namespaced skill references and one relative link to `../using-superpowers/`. This dropped piece is dead in an installed environment. Re-porting under the adaptation filter would fix them; the operator chose fidelity over local correctness. Drift handling for this piece is re-mirror, not judge-and-adapt.
localDeltas: SKILL.md frontmatter `description`: adds "auditing existing skills" to the trigger list (upstream reads "Use when creating new skills, editing existing skills, or verifying skills work before deployment"). Operator call: auditing an existing skill is a distinct trigger from editing one, and the description is the activation surface. Re-apply after every re-mirror.
